messages:
Sean Gallagher: need to lock rollout SLO gates for profile pack canary. what blocks rollout vs just creates a ticket. also kill-switch semantics are still fuzzy.

Rafael Mendes: +1. we can’t ship this without crisp “stop the line” criteria.

Allison Grant: I can wire alerts either way, but need thresholds + which dashboards are required for go/no-go.

Neha Kapoor: reminder: Hosted canary includes mixed workloads. gates must catch tail latency regressions + elevated 5xx/timeouts.

Sean Gallagher: proposal draft (feel free to shred):
- Phase 0: internal canary (1% traffic, 2 regions)
- Phase 1: broader canary (5%)
Gates evaluated per SKU (H100/L40S) and per route (chat/generate/embeddings) where possible.

Mateo Alvarez: ok. runtime team wants gates that don’t block on noise though. we saw variance in p99 last week.

Sofia Ivanova: can we gate on queueing time instead of end-to-end only? scheduler changes will show up there earlier.

Caleb Johnson: we now have `scheduler_queue_ms` histogram tagged by `profile_id` + `sku` in the branch. should be in prod once 1.22 lands.

Allison Grant: if we do queueing: what’s the acceptable delta? also careful about cardinality if we split too much.

Rafael Mendes: let’s split into paging vs ticket:
PAGING (hard stop, auto-disable canary)
1) p99 E2E latency regression > 15% vs control for 10m (same cohort)
2) 5xx rate > 0.5% or timeout rate > 0.3% for 5m on canary cohort
3) OOM / restart loop: >3 container restarts per host per 15m correlated with canary
TICKET (non-blocking but investigate)
- kernel fallback rate > baseline + 2% for 30m
- KV compaction time p95 > baseline + 25% for 30m
- queueing p95 elevated but E2E stable

Sean Gallagher: I like the shape. but we need definitions. p99 of what? request latency? token latency?

Omar El-Sayed: for “generate/chat” we have:
- `request_latency_ms` (end-to-end)
- `prefill_ms` and `decode_ms` in traces (not everywhere yet)
- `stream_first_token_ms` (TTFT)
- `tokens_per_sec` counters
SLO gates should probably be E2E + TTFT, otherwise a batching change can keep E2E ok but TTFT gets ugly.

Allison Grant: agree. paging gate should include TTFT p99 too, esp for interactive.

Neha Kapoor: can we have separate gates for chat vs batch routes? embeddings shouldn’t page on TTFT.

Rafael Mendes: yes. route buckets:
- interactive (chat/generate streaming): gate on TTFT p99 + E2E p99
- batch (non-streaming generate): gate on E2E p99 + throughput drop
- embeddings: gate on error + p95 latency only

Connor O'Brien: release requirement: gates must be written down + in the go/no-go checklist. also who can hit kill switch?

Sean Gallagher: kill switch semantics:
- Immediate: disable feature flag `runtime.profile_pack.enabled` for cohort (Hosted control plane)
- Rollback: set `profile_version=previous` for canary pool (or revert default selection)
Question: does disable mean “ignore pack entirely” or “use pack but pin last-known-good”? need deterministic.

Mateo Alvarez: disable should mean “fall back to legacy defaults” (pre-pack behavior). otherwise we’re stuck if pack itself is bad.

Sofia Ivanova: careful: if we disable, we also lose a bunch of the new guardrails (admission control tuned per profile). might be ok for emergency but expect load-shed differences.

Neha Kapoor: for incident response, clarity beats purity. disable = go back to last stable behavior. we can accept losing guardrails in exchange for restoring known baseline.

Caleb Johnson: implementation note: we can structure as:
- if flag off => use legacy config path
- if flag on => load pack + selection
- separate knob `profile_version_pin` for Dedicated/Private
So kill switch (Hosted) is flipping the flag. For Dedicated we should probably not auto-flip without customer consent.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Hosted gets auto-disable on paging gates. Dedicated gets “page SRE + runtime” but action is manual + comms.

Allison Grant: ok, alert routing:
- Hosted canary cohort (tag `cohort=profilepack_canary`): paging on gates (PD)
- Non-canary / rest of fleet: ticket only unless it breaches global SLO
Need exact threshold values to encode.

Sean Gallagher: let’s pin values:
HOSTED CANARY (interactive routes)
- TTFT p99 regression > 20% vs control for 10m => PAGE + auto-disable
- E2E p99 regression > 15% vs control for 10m => PAGE + auto-disable
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts) > 0.5% for 5m => PAGE + auto-disable
HOSTED CANARY (all routes)
- GPU OOM events > 0 in 5m AND correlated with canary hosts => PAGE + auto-disable

TICKET thresholds:
- kernel fallback rate > 1% absolute for 30m (per SKU) => ticket
- scheduler_queue_ms p95 > 2x baseline for 30m => ticket (unless also drives E2E)
- fragmentation_estimate > 0.2 sustained 60m => ticket

Omar El-Sayed: “OOM events” — we can alert on `cuda_oom_total` counter + restart count. correlation is messy but we can scope alert to canary pool labels.

Allison Grant: for kernel fallback: do we expect >0 on B200 bring-up? we might see higher during early access.

Neha Kapoor: this thread is specifically for profile pack canary on H100/L40S in Hosted. B200 is separate bring-up plan; different gates.

Talia Benson: capturing these as action items. will add to rollout checklist doc + link in ENG-4933.

Connor O'Brien: for go/no-go: include “auto-disable tested in staging” as a requirement. we’ve been burned by kill switches that don’t actually flip.

Rafael Mendes: yep. can we simulate a breach by lowering threshold temporarily? or run a manual “disable canary” drill.

Caleb Johnson: we can add a `/admin/flags` endpoint check in staging + a runbook step: flip flag, confirm runtime logs show `profile_pack_enabled=false` and `legacy_config=true`.

Sean Gallagher: also need comms semantics: if auto-disable happens, what gets posted where? I want:
- #incidents if paging
- #eng-runtime and #eng-sre notification
- include: cohort, sku, profile_version, delta, link to dashboard

Allison Grant: I can configure PD to post a summary to Slack via webhook. just need the fields. we have `profile_id`, `profile_version`, `sku` tags now.

Mateo Alvarez: last ask: don’t page on single region blips. can we require 2 regions OR require control vs canary delta not absolute threshold?

Rafael Mendes: we already use delta vs control for latency. for errors, we can require both: canary error > 0.5% AND (canary/control) > 2x for 5m.

Sean Gallagher: done. I’ll write this up in the SRE rollout guardrails page. Allison can you draft the alert definitions w/ labels? Caleb: confirm tags will be in 1.22.

Allison Grant: yep, will draft alert spec today. will mark paging vs ticket explicitly.

Caleb Johnson: confirmed tags are in pr-24935 + pr-25014. should be in next nightly.

Neha Kapoor: ok. once doc is up, please link it in release go/no-go email thread too.
